finding: The module is named after the most overloaded word in a website builder - every element on a page is content - while its actual object is CMS collections plus three data primitives, and the front door names neither.
evidence: 148:2 has 21 text nodes: 'Content', 'COLLECTIONS 2', five rows, 'DATA', three rows. No purpose line. The one sentence that explains the object exists only on the empty state 149:7 - 'Collections turn a spreadsheet into pages - one page per row, updated when the data changes.' - so it is seen once and never again. The code already knows the truth: rail/tabsConfig.ts:245-246 sets label 'Content' but ariaLabel 'Data sources and collections for dynamic content'.
recommend: Promote 149:7's sentence to a persistent purpose line on 148:2, and put the rail label question to the founder - 'Data' or 'Collections' names the object; 'Content' names everything.

finding: All five navigable rows carry an identical plus-sign icon, so nothing distinguishes a collection from a variable list - and the one row that actually creates something uses a different glyph.
evidence: Non-text inventory of 148:2: rows at y 84/116/212/244/276 each hold FRAME 'icon' > INSTANCE 'glyph' > a 14x0 plus 0x14 VECTOR pair (a plus). The 'New collection' row at y146 instead uses a TEXT '+' at 147,16. Shipped code already distinguishes them - ContentViews.tsx:204-206 uses Database / Braces / GitBranch.
recommend: Take the shipped icon set into the board. A leading plus on a row that navigates contradicts the trailing chevron on the same row.

finding: The 'New collection' row is wired to the field editor of a collection that does not exist yet, and the real creation modal has no entry point other than a debug hotspot.
evidence: Reaction carrier 'Row . New collection' on 148:2 navigates to 151:2 'Content . fields', whose own back link reads '< Menu items . fields' - a drill-in of an existing collection. 1170:4713 'Content . collection-setup (modal)' is reachable only from 'hotspot/state . Content . collection-set' on 149:50, i.e. from inside a collection you already have.
recommend: Rewire 'New collection' to 1170:4713. As drawn, the prototype cannot demonstrate the module's first action.

finding: 'Dynamic pages' - the feature the module's own empty state promises - is an unwired row leading to a screen that exists in the product and nowhere in the file.
evidence: 149:50's 'Dynamic pages >' row sits at y786 and carries no reaction; the frame's four reactions go to record, collection-setup, unsaved-record and collection.empty. The product ships it as its own drill-in with back and save: ContentTab.tsx:299-318, ContentView kind 'dynamic-pages' (useContentPanel.ts:28), backed by cms.generateDynamicPages (cms.ts:92) and collection.pageSlugPattern. A name search across all 27 sections for /dynamic|slug pattern/ returns NONE.
recommend: Board 'Content . dynamic-pages': the slug-pattern field, the template picker, the SEO-title pattern, the preview of what will be generated, and the result. 1170:4713 draws a one-line version of this inside the setup modal; the standalone screen is where a user changes it later.

finding: Two record lists ship for the same collection, and only one of them can publish, import or delete - so a user must already know which surface to open to do the job.
evidence: 149:50 is a 280px drill-in listing records with a chevron each and an '+ Add' link. 1170:4749 is a 640px modal listing the same records with per-row Unpublish / edit / delete, plus 'Import JSON' and '+ Add record'. Both ship: ContentTab.tsx case 'collection' and editor/shell/modals/CMSRecordsModal.tsx.
recommend: Decide which is the record list. If the modal stays, the panel row list needs a visible door to it; if the panel stays, it needs the modal's actions. Two lists with different powers and no cross-reference is the shape users describe as 'I could do this yesterday'.

finding: A condition is a property of one element, and it lives in a site-level data panel where the element it belongs to is not visible - while the Inspector, whose whole job is element properties, has no conditions section at all.
evidence: ConditionsView rows are keyed by elementId and the only way to see the subject is a menu item that selects it on canvas (ContentViews.tsx:1044-1096, onSelectElement). Board 151:87 shows 'Happy hour banner / when time is 17:00-19:00' with no indication of which element that is. A grep of editor/inspector for conditions returns only field.conditional - the renderer's own predicate, an unrelated concept.
recommend: Move the per-element condition editor into the Inspector (section 1776:8381) and keep at most a read-only 'conditions on this page' list in Content. Recommend a rename of 151:87 rather than a delete, per the standing rule.

finding: The two structural actions for a collection are pinned below a 520px void, and the board does not say what happens to them once the record list is longer than the panel.
evidence: 149:50: records occupy y118-230 (4 rows) while the header says '24 records'; 'Fields >' sits at y754 and 'Dynamic pages >' at y786, flush to the 812px panel's bottom edge. At the stated 24 records the list scrolls and the board is silent on whether the two rows stay pinned or scroll away with it.
recommend: Draw the scrolled variant. Either pin the two rows as a footer and say so, or move them up under the header where they read as part of the collection rather than as leftovers.

finding: The loading board states a count it cannot yet know.
evidence: 775:4241 renders 'COLLECTIONS' with the badge '2' at 52,252 and 'DATA' while every row is a skeleton. The Layers module has already ruled on this exact question in code - LayersTab.tsx:213-216, 'a count of a list that did not load is not a fact' - and drops its footer count on failure.
recommend: Skeleton the badge with the rows, or drop it. A number over a skeleton is the one part of a loading state a user will believe.

finding: A user can create a collection and has no way to remove it. The delete exists at every layer except the one the user can reach.
evidence: server/trpc/routers/cms.ts:69 exposes collections.delete; services/cmsSync.ts:197 calls it; engine/cms/CollectionManager.ts:154 and CollectionStorage.ts:129 implement it. A grep of all of packages/editor/src for a UI caller of deleteCollection / collections.delete returns nothing outside those files - no button, no menu item, no board. 148:2's rows carry a chevron and no overflow menu; 149:50's header carries '+ Add' and no menu.
recommend: Board and build collection delete, with the consequence stated: deleting a collection takes its records and any pages generated from it. This is the missing door pattern - a full stack with no handle on the front.

finding: The modal deletes a record with no confirmation, while the panel's record screen confirms the same delete - and the module has no board for any of the three confirms the code already ships.
evidence: CMSRecordsModal.tsx:154 calls composer.cms.collections.deleteContentItem(id) directly; a grep of that file for Confirm/confirm returns nothing. ContentViews.tsx:381 wraps the panel's record delete in ConfirmDialog, :573 confirms a field delete, :306 confirms leaving with unsaved changes. No Content board draws any of the three. I did not verify whether a CMS record delete is undoable.
recommend: One delete contract for both surfaces, and board the three confirms that already exist. A destructive action that is guarded on one screen and bare on another teaches users the wrong lesson about both.

finding: Implementation notes and prototype hotspots are rendered as visible board content, so the board cannot be read as a design.
evidence: 1170:4749 carries a body-text footnote at 310,16 - 'Width stays 640: F15 adds the matching kind to Modal.tsx KIND_WIDTH. The code renders this at ModalContent lg (720) today.' - and its four state hotspots sit at y238 INSIDE the modal body, overlapping the Tiramisu row (the render shows 'Publish' colliding with 'publish-error'). Sibling boards park their hotspot strip outside the frame at y828. Board 1717:17217 has the same defect with an aria/CSS note as body text.
recommend: Move notes to Figma comments or the Notes section and the hotspot strip below the frame, as the other 58 boards in these four modules already do.

finding: The default tree draws a permanent, unchecked checkbox column that the product deliberately hides - and if the checkboxes were always visible, the module's separate bulk-select board would not be a distinct state.
evidence: Non-text inventory of 140:2: six INSTANCE 'Checkbox' at x=16 on every row (y 88,120,152,184,216,248), visible and unchecked in the render, sitting left of the folder chevron at x=40. PageRow.tsx:6-7: 'The bd-pg-panel.bulk-mode parent gates the row checkbox via CSS; this component always renders the checkbox slot.' The code is right - a selection column ahead of the page name on a six-row list is noise.
recommend: Take the checkboxes off 140:2 and let 141:78 own them. That also restores bulk-select as a state worth a board.

finding: The bulk action bar's labels overlap into unreadable text, and there is no visible way to leave the selection.
evidence: 141:78: 'Duplicate' at x=96 and 'Move to...' at x=126 - 30px apart for a ~55px label; the render reads 'DuplMoveate to...'. Three actions plus a '3 selected' count do not fit a 280px bar. No Cancel, no x, no 'Clear' anywhere in the band; the shipped exit is the Escape key alone (PagesTab.tsx:131-133), which nothing on screen announces.
recommend: Re-lay the bar for 280px - the count on its own line, or Duplicate and Move behind an overflow - and add a visible dismiss. Escape as the only exit from a mode with a Delete button in it is not an exit.

screen: Page delete has no confirm board
finding: The module's two destructive paths both ship a confirmation dialog and neither has a board, in a file where nine other modules have one.
evidence: PagesTab.tsx:122 opens a single-page delete confirm (setDeleteTargetId); :345-349 opens a bulk one that names every page and adds 'One undo (Cmd-Z) brings them all back'. A name search across all 27 sections for /delet|confirm|discard|remove/ returns 29 frames - Media, History x3, Publish x2, Review x2, Compare x2, Inspector, Templates, Notifications - and none in Pages.
recommend: Board both. The bulk one already has the best confirm copy in the product written for it in code; it should be design's, not a comment's.

finding: The module's only inline-error board draws a Pages panel that no other board in the module draws, so building it would produce two different Pages panels.
evidence: 1717:17217 is 280x320 where all twelve siblings are 280x812; its header is 'PAGES' 11px Semi Bold at 12,12 against the siblings' 'Pages' 11px Medium at 14,16; it has no search box, no 'Listings' toggle, no folders and no '+ Add page' footer, using a bare '+' at 10,258 instead; and it renders an implementation note as visible body text at y268 ('role=alert aria-live=assertive . .bd-pg-name-error, 11px --bk-error. The commit is refused; the row stays...').
recommend: Redraw the conflict as an inline error on 140:2's own row rhythm. As it stands the module's error state is the one board a builder must not copy.

finding: A four-column SEO table is drawn inside a 280px drawer where three of its four columns truncate, the view has no way back, and its footer link promises a destination it does not go to.
evidence: 141:207 renders PAGE / TITLE / DESC / SCORE at 280px as 'Bella C...', 'Our me...', 'Contac...'. The 'Listings' toggle at 54,192 shows no active state while the panel is in the listings view, and the board draws no back control - the shipped panel had to add a '< Pages' link (PagesTab.tsx:251-258). 'Open full listings >' is wired to onExpandToggle (PagesTab.tsx:260), which widens this same panel; the chevron reads as navigation.
recommend: Draw the expanded variant as the real listings screen and make the 280px version a summary, or drop the DESC column at drawer width. Either way the board needs the back affordance the code invented for it.

finding: The error state keeps its primary create action live over a list that failed to load.
evidence: 141:165 shows 'Couldn't load your pages.' / 'The site is fine - this panel isn't.' / 'Try again' and still renders '+ Add page' at y752. Adding a page to a list whose current contents are unknown is the one action a load failure should take away - the same reasoning the Layers module applies to its footer count (LayersTab.tsx:213-216).
recommend: Disable or remove '+ Add page' on 141:165. 'Try again' is the only action this screen has a right to offer.

finding: A piece of canvas chrome is filed inside the Pages panel section, which distorts the module's screen count and its coverage.
evidence: 435:2348 is 1080x920 where all twelve siblings are 280x812, and its name self-identifies as PageTabBar.tsx - the tab strip above the canvas, not a panel screen. Its only reactions go to Journeys / S1 . Editor.
recommend: Re-file into Shell (1776:8385) where the topbar and canvas chrome live. Recommend a move, not a delete.

finding: The board asserts a chord in its own name that the shell command palette also owns, so the screen it draws is not the only thing that opens.
evidence: The finder is real and shipping - PagesTab.tsx:126-129 binds Cmd-K on window and opens PageCommandPalette, which the board matches (a 256-wide dropdown anchored in the panel, 'go to page...' placeholder, name + home glyph rows). Per the coordinator's cross-module finding, StudioHeader.tsx:250 binds Cmd-K on document for the shell palette and neither listener stops propagation, so with Pages mounted one Cmd-K opens both.
recommend: Not re-filed here - the chord collision belongs to the cross-module row. What this module owes is a decision recorded on the board: either the Pages finder takes a different chord, or the board says it is the shell palette scoped to pages.

finding: Nothing on the Pages panel says what it is for, in the file or in the product, while its sibling tree has just been given a line.
evidence: 140:2's text is 'Pages', 'Search', 'Listings', the folder rows, '+ Add page' - no purpose copy. A grep of PagesTab.tsx for a purpose or subtitle line returns nothing, whereas panels/layers/index.tsx:388 now ships 'Every element on this page. Drag a row to reorder or nest it.'
recommend: Give Pages the same one line. See D-F-21 for why this one matters more than it looks.

finding: The two structure panels are near-identical on arrival, so nothing on either screen tells a user which tree answers which question.
evidence: Both are 280x812; both open with an 11px Medium title at 14,16 ('Layers' / 'Pages'); both put a search box at y~52; both list eight rows on a 28-32px pitch with a leading glyph and trailing row controls; neither board carries a purpose line. The only differentiator is the title word - and 'Layers' is a designer's word, not a small-business owner's. The product has fixed exactly one side: panels/layers/index.tsx:388.
recommend: Board the Layers line, write the Pages one, and make the two visually distinguishable at a glance - the page tree wants page-shaped rows (slug, home marker, status), the layer tree wants element-shaped ones. A one-word difference is not an information architecture.

finding: The board's UNBUILDABLE label is right about the condition and the product shipped the screen anyway - so the empty state now appears when there is no page at all, saying 'This page is empty'.
evidence: The frame name asserts that buildLayersFromEngine always emits a root row, so layers.length===0 means no page or composer, never an empty page. That is correct: useLayerTree.ts ends setLayers([buildTree(rootElement, 0)]) and returns [] only when composer, page or rootElement is missing. index.tsx:431 renders LayersEmptyState on state.layers.length === 0, and LayersEmptyState.tsx:21/:32 carries this board's exact copy - 'This page is empty. Drop something on the canvas to see it here.' and 'Open Insert'. An empty page yields one row (the root), not zero.
recommend: Keep the screen, fix its copy for the state it actually fires in ('No page open' / 'Nothing to show yet'), and rename the frame to drop the UNBUILDABLE claim once the copy is right. A board named unbuildable that shipped verbatim is how a stale label survives.

finding: Eleven of the twelve tree boards start at 'Section' and omit the root row the engine always emits, so every row-position, indent and count measured off them is one row out.
evidence: useLayerTree.ts closes buildLayersFromEngine with setLayers([buildTree(rootElement, 0)]) - the page root is always element 0 - and index.tsx:440 maps filteredLayers straight into LayerTreeItem with no depth-0 skip. Only 1082:4640 'Layers . expanded' draws it ('Page' at 86,40, footer '24 layers'). 142:2, 143:2, 143:60, 143:119, 143:179, 143:237, 143:295, 775:4130, 1082:4527, 1082:4589 and 1171:4829 all begin at Section.
recommend: Add the root row to the eleven, or decide it should be suppressed and change useLayerTree. Right now the module's most-copied board and its own expanded variant disagree about what row 1 is.

finding: Drag supports three drop positions and the module boards one of them - the two that nest are undrawn, including the one the shipped purpose line advertises.
evidence: The render of 143:60 shows a single blue insertion line between 'Button' and 'Gallery' (the text dump's 2px shift at y196->198) - a sibling reorder. panels/layers/types.ts:56 defines 'before' | 'after' | 'inside', and index.tsx:388 now tells users 'Drag a row to reorder or nest it'. No board shows the inside drop: no indent cue, no parent highlight, and no answer to how a user aims at a third target inside a 28px row.
recommend: Board the inside drop and the aiming zones. This is the module's headline interaction and two thirds of it has never been designed.

finding: The module's only error-affordance board is unreadable: its explanation is clipped mid-sentence and a spec annotation is drawn on top of the tree rows.
evidence: The render clips the tooltip to 'A button can't contain a' where the text node at 199,12 reads 'A button can't contain a section'. Separately, '(empty slot - reserved so selecting a row cannot reflow the tree)' is rendered at 91,12 inside the panel, overlapping the Section and Container rows.
recommend: Size the tooltip to its copy or shorten the copy, and move the slot note out of the artwork. A rule about what cannot nest is worth nothing if the noun is cut off.

finding: Three of the popover's four labels clip inside their own popover, and the shipped popover offers a different set of options - neither set contains the other.
evidence: The render shows 'Show hidden la...', 'Show lock badg...', 'Highlight CMS-t...'. Board options: Show hidden layers / Show lock badges / Compact rows / Highlight CMS-bound. LayerDisplaySettings.tsx ships Show HTML tags ('div, section, h1...') / Show element IDs ('#abc123 format') / Compact rows, under a 'Display Settings' header with a close x the board does not draw. One option in common out of four and three.
recommend: Settle the set, then size the popover to it. The board's options are the user-facing ones; the code's two extras are developer concepts sitting in a no-code builder's layer panel and belong behind a dev toggle if anywhere.

finding: A per-row badge is boarded as a screen, which the file has already ruled against for the identical case one board over.
evidence: 143:237's text content is byte-identical to 142:2 - same eight rows, same '12 layers' footer; only a glyph fill differs. 1082:4739 is named 'Layers . component-instance - NOT A STATE - a per-row badge gated on composer.components.isInstance', which is the same argument. 143:179 'hidden' is a near-twin but does add a breadcrumb line at 90,12 ('Container / Paragraph') that appears on no other tree board, though LayerBreadcrumb.tsx ships.
recommend: One 'Layers . row states' board showing hidden, locked and instance on different rows at once, and a decision on whether the breadcrumb belongs on every tree board or none. Recommend renaming 143:237, not deleting it.

finding: Four boards of the same list give four different answers about the footer count, and the two that print a number print one they cannot know.
evidence: 775:4130 (loading) prints '12 layers' over seven skeleton rows. 143:2 (filtered) prints '12 layers' with one matching row. 782:4260 (no-results) prints nothing. 781:4217 (load-error) prints nothing. The code states the rule for one case only - LayersTab.tsx:213-216, count dropped when the tree failed, 'a count of a list that did not load is not a fact' - which condemns the loading board by the same sentence, and 143:295 already proves the filtered form exists ('3 selected of 12').
recommend: One footer contract across all six list states: skeleton while loading, 'n of m' while filtered, absent on failure.

finding: The menu offers an action nothing backs and that a shipped pair of actions already performs.
evidence: Board menu: Cut, Copy, Paste, Duplicate, Delete, Rename, Group selection, Move to page..., Copy link. LayerContextMenu.tsx:57-59 - 'Move to page... and Copy link wait for real backing - a dead item is worse than a missing one'; Copy link was later built (:81), Move to page... was not, on the grounds that 'cut/paste already crosses pages'. The shipped order also differs (Copy link is fourth, not ninth).
recommend: Drop 'Move to page...' from the board or specify what it does that cut-then-paste does not, and align the two orders so the board and the menu can be compared.

finding: The expanded variant uses a header no sibling uses, so the module's one correct tree is also its one inconsistent chrome.
evidence: 1082:4640 draws 'Layers' at 14px Semi Bold with a refresh and close control at 14,241 / 14,255; every other Layers board draws 'Layers' at 11px Medium with no header controls. It is also the only board that draws the root row (see D-F-23) and the only one with a 24-layer tree.
recommend: Reconcile the header with the rest of the module, or state that expanded is a different surface with its own chrome. It cannot be both the reference tree and the outlier.

finding: The panel makes a safety promise about undo that is true of one of its two paths, printed directly above the control that starts the other one.
evidence: 170:2 carries 'AI proposes a diff and never writes directly. Apply lands as one undo step.' at 304,16 (inside a FRAME named note), and the product renders it as real UI copy - EmptyThread.tsx:53. AgentPlan.tsx:30-33 states the multi-step contract: 'each approved step applies in its own transaction (applySetStyle opens one per edit), so a three-step run is three undo entries.' The sentence sits immediately above the DRAFT row that launches that multi-step run, and 171:67's own footer says the opposite - 'Each step applies on its own - Cmd-Z takes back the last one, Undo all takes back every step.'
recommend: Rewrite the idle promise to be true of both paths, or scope it ('a chat edit lands as one undo step; a multi-step run lands as one per step'). This is an AI surface editing an agency's client site - the undo guarantee is the thing a user leans on before pressing Apply, and right now it is wrong in the direction that costs them.

finding: The one state where the user is waiting on a model has no way to stop it and no way back - and the product already has the control the board is missing.
evidence: 170:29's only reaction is frame -> AI . planning; the render shows 'Thinking...' in a tinted band with no control of any kind, while 170:41 (planning) and 170:70 (running) both draw 'Stop' at 349,60. Composer.tsx:44-45 renders a Stop button whenever streaming is true.
recommend: Draw the Stop on 170:29. Code is right; the board is the one that would teach a rebuilder to ship a dead-end wait.

finding: Three terminal states draw a live Stop button, and one of them contradicts itself about whether the run happened.
evidence: 'Stop' is drawn at 349,60 on 171:67 (all three steps ticked, band 'DONE . 3 OF 3'), 171:36 ('STOPPED BY YOU') and 171:2 ('STOPPED AT STEP 2'). AgentPlan.tsx:176 gates it correctly: (phase === 'running' || phase === 'planning'). Separately 171:67 shows three completed steps and then a card reading '3 changes proposed' with Discard and Apply - so the board says the steps both ran and are pending.
recommend: Remove Stop from the three terminal boards, and settle whether a finished run has applied its steps or proposed them. As drawn, the module's success screen cannot be read.

finding: Every board in the module is 60px wider than the column the panel actually renders in, so every measurement taken off them is wrong.
evidence: All eleven AI frames are 360x776 (170:2, 170:17, 170:29, 170:41, 170:70, 170:97, 171:2, 171:36, 171:67, 171:105, 171:136). The panel renders in the inspector column - StudioPanels.tsx:298 setAiInInspector(true), :495 - and themes/tokens.generated.css:131 sets --bk-size-inspector: 300px. AITab.css:1-6 gives .bd-ai-tab no width of its own, so it fills 300.
recommend: Redraw at 300, or change the token. The boards' own '< Inspector' back link at 8,16 proves they know which column they are in.

finding: A band's value is boarded as a screen, and the change it draws is one the product does not make and should not.
evidence: 170:17 differs from 170:2 only in the band text ('Scope: Hero section' vs 'Scope: Page') and by dropping the TRY and DRAFT sections entirely. ScopeChip.tsx renders that band on every state ('Every AI board opens the panel with a tinted band reading Scope: <what>'), and EmptyThread renders TRY plus DRAFT whenever the thread is empty, regardless of scope - so the removal is not what ships.
recommend: Fold 170:17 into 170:2 as the scope band's second value. Taking the suggestions away at the moment a user has just selected an element removes help exactly when the request is most specific.

screen: No board shows a second turn
finding: The shipped surface is a conversation and not one of the eleven boards shows two turns of it.
evidence: ChatThread.tsx maps a messages array into ChatMessage components and scrolls on change (:23, :35-36); DiffRows.tsx renders per-message diffs; AITab wires the thread. All eleven boards draw exactly one prompt and one response. Nothing shows a thread with prior turns, a scrolled thread, a message you can re-run, what a rejected diff leaves behind, or where a second prompt goes while a run is live.
recommend: Board the multi-turn thread, including the case that matters most: the user types again while a run is going. That is the state an assistant panel spends most of its life in and it has never been drawn.

finding: Both dead-end states offer exactly one action, and neither action goes anywhere - each returns to the empty prompt it came from.
evidence: 171:105's only control is 'See plans' (258,16) and 171:136's is 'Open workspace settings' (220,16). Each frame carries a single reaction, both to AI . idle. Neither reaches Settings/S7 (1776:8387), which exists in the same file. The states themselves are real - ai.getQuotaStatus (ai.ts:273) backs the first and a missing OPENAI_API_KEY backs the second.
recommend: Wire 'Open workspace settings' into the Settings section and decide where 'See plans' lands - billing is a dashboard surface, so this may be an outbound link and should be drawn as one. A screen whose only button returns you to the screen you could not use is a dead end with a button on it.

finding: Four ai router procedures and the three pages translation procedures have no board in these modules, and none of them should - recording it so the next audit does not re-file them.
evidence: ai.summarize has no editor caller (FormsScreen.tsx:405's summarize is a local function). ai.milestoneSuggest reaches HistoryTab via useAutoMilestone.ts:180 - History's module. ai.componentSchema is consumed by engine/designSystem/services/ComponentSchemaAIClient.ts - Brand's. ai.logAdoption is telemetry (services/ai/adoptionTracker.ts:25). pages.getTranslation / setTranslation / removeTranslation (pages.ts:71-90) have no editor-side caller at all - the D-X-07 precedent applies: a router without an editor surface is not an editor design gap.
recommend: No action, except that pages translations is worth a founder question - three procedures with no door anywhere is either a dashboard feature or an abandoned one.
